title: Bromohydrin from 2-methylpropene
subtitle: Water opens the bromonium ion

reactants.caption: 2-methylpropene + bromine in water
reactants.learnerPrompt: Bromine meets the alkene. Draw the first step.
hintTiers: As with any alkene and Br₂: what three-membered ring forms first?
The π bond attacks the near bromine, a lone pair of that bromine bonds to the other alkene carbon, and the Br–Br bond breaks. Three arrows.
Arrow 1: from the C=C π bond to the near bromine. Arrow 2: from a lone pair of that bromine to the other alkene carbon. Arrow 3: from the Br–Br bond onto the far bromine.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Water and the alkene are both nucleophiles. The alkene reacts with bromine first.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: That gives an open tertiary cation. With bromine, a lone pair of the attached bromine bonds to the other carbon at the same time: a bromonium ion.
Add one more arrow: a lone pair of the attached bromine bonds to the other alkene carbon, closing a three-membered ring.

bromonium-ion.caption: the bromonium ion + bromide, in water
bromonium-ion.learnerPrompt: Water opens the bromonium ion. Which carbon does it attack?
hintTiers: Water is the solvent, so it wins over bromide. Which ring carbon carries more positive charge?
Water attacks the more substituted (tertiary) carbon, and that C–Br bond breaks onto the bromine. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: from a water lone pair to the ring carbon bearing two methyl groups. Arrow 2: from the bond between that carbon and the ring bromine onto the bromine.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Not the CH₂ carbon. The bond from bromine to the tertiary carbon is longer and weaker, and that carbon carries more positive charge, so water attacks there, even though it is more hindered.
Bromide can open the ring (giving the dibromide), but water is the solvent and vastly outnumbers bromide. Use water.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right carbon. It now has five bonds: break its bond to the ring bromine.

oxonium.caption: protonated bromohydrin (an oxonium ion)
hintTiers: The oxygen is positive and carries two H atoms. What can take one?
A second water molecule takes a proton from the oxonium oxygen. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: from a lone pair of the free water to an H on the oxonium oxygen. Arrow 2: from that O–H bond onto the oxonium oxygen.

steps.explanationAfterStep: An unsymmetrical bromonium ion: the bond from bromine to the tertiary carbon is the weaker one.
Water attacks the tertiary carbon from the face opposite the bromine (anti addition). The transition state has a lot of cation character, so the carbon that holds positive charge best reacts.
The bromohydrin: OH on the more substituted carbon, Br on the less substituted one.

mechanismSummary: Bromine forms a bromonium ion with the alkene. In water, water is the nucleophile in huge excess and opens the ring at the more substituted carbon, which carries more of the positive charge. A second water removes the proton: 1-bromo-2-methylpropan-2-ol, with Br on the CH₂ carbon and OH on the tertiary carbon.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 20
